tasks.short: Review remote baggage images and alert screeners

steps.what: View checked-bag and cargo images using remote screening equipment
Alert baggage screeners or handlers to possible problems

tasks.design: Keep image interpretation with the authorised screener using existing {OTHER} remote screening equipment. The screener communicates the relevant observation and bag or cargo reference through {TELEPHONY}; no model-generated problem assessment is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Image content and its association with the physical item require reliable interpretation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing remote equipment supports review, but the digest establishes no new validated image-analysis capability for this task.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguous images and ensuring the alert reaches the right handling team.
tasks.human_edge: The screener can explain uncertainty and seek the authorised next check.
tasks.altitude: Image-review and alerting responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.task: Confirm the item associated with a screening alert
reach.learn: Use the authorised item reference and acknowledge uncertainty

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: remote baggage image interpretation and contextual alerting require task-specific competence; generic detection tools do not establish equivalent capability.

assumptions: Boundary is remote image review and alerting, excluding image acquisition, physical bag location and inspection. European operator and national procedures define authority.

Existing screening operator and equipment produce image and associated item reference before s1. Screener verifies their association and interprets content in s1's 70 hours, then communicates and confirms receipt in s2's 30 hours. Missing or inconsistent references trigger manual escalation; no structured suspicious-item flag is presumed.
Review existing approved equipment configuration before adding software; current image transfer runtime earns no labour saving.
Zero incremental upkeep because no new technology or procedure is introduced.
unknowns: Approved remote-review equipment and competence requirements
How alerts and item references are acknowledged
research_questions: Where do item-reference or acknowledgement failures cause repeated screening communication?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross and net=0. Image interpretation and live alerting retain all their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Locate and set aside bags identified for inspection

steps.what: Locate suspicious bags by matching the remote printout to physical baggage
Set the identified bags aside for authorised inspection

tasks.design: Keep physical bag identification and segregation with the screener. An existing {OTHER} baggage tracking system may be a reference, but an electronic message does not establish that the correct physical bag has been found.
tasks.previous_blocker: Remote information must be matched to a physical item in the handling area.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing references can support the match; no additional physical automation is established.
tasks.still_hard: Unreadable references, similar bags and discrepancies between the printout and handling area.
tasks.human_edge: The screener recognises an uncertain match and avoids treating it as confirmed.
tasks.altitude: The physical identification and handover duty remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Communicate the item reference and unresolved discrepancies

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: locating and physically segregating a specific bag requires reliable item matching and on-site handling.

assumptions: Boundary starts with an existing remote screening printout and ends at inspection handover; remote image review and actual inspection are separately owned.

Remote screening staff produce the printout and associated item reference before this task. Screener performs the physical comparison in s1's counted 60 hours; uncertain or absent references require manual clarification before s2. No automatically produced matched-bag flag is assumed.
Test existing approved tracking references before new tools; existing tracking runtime earns no new labour saving.
Zero upkeep because no new tool, field or handling process is proposed.
unknowns: Reliability of the printed item reference
research_questions: How often does an unclear printout prevent a confident physical item match?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross and net=0. Physical matching, movement and handover retain their effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Maintain competent image review and reliable physical item association without adding unvalidated automated clearance.
reach: Give baggage handlers and inspectors traceable item-reference handovers
role.ambitious_version: A screener whose observations and item handovers remain clear enough for authorised personnel to act on confidently.
